items.Sentence: Primary treatment consists of 2-millimeter (mm) drum screens with a bypass channel/bar with screens and a vortex grit removal mechanism.

Wastewater flows from the primary treatment units into two main bioreactor trains used for secondary treatment. Each bioreactor train consists of two anoxic zones followed by one aerobic zone with two aeration grids.
Flow from the aerobic zone is pumped to the membrane filtration units, which provide tertiary treatment.
The tertiary-treated effluent is disinfected using an ultraviolet light (UV) disinfection system.
After detainment in the digester, the solids are sent to dewatering equipment, which includes a centrifuge.
Following the interchange tanks, the reduced solids are purged into the digester, which holds the solids for 10 to 15 days.
The dewatered biosolids are hauled off-site to the Clovis Municipal Solid Waste Landfill.
As a backup option, the biosolids could be hauled to a Class B Solids land application facility or a composting facility.
A second 3.08 MG bolted-steel tank will be added with the completion of Phase II, as described in section II.E of this Fact Sheet.
